text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Parliament's financial and fiscal specialists to decide today on inquiry of government's fiscal support of Philips Electronics and Fokker. (p1)
- Planned bio-ethanol project will not go through unless junior finance minister Wim Vermeend exempts it from excise duty. (p1)
- Wholesaler group Sligro Beheer boosts 1996 net by 21 pct to Dfl 19.7 million; Sligro forecasts autonomous turnover growth. (p3)
- Nutricia's salmonella worries extend to France.(p3)
- Philips Electronics cuts 325 of the 730 jobs at its headoffice in Eindhoven. (p3)
- Food concern CSM announces that the recently bought U.S. Karp's will contribute to this year's earnings. (p5)
- Dutch government will not stop Heinekin brewing beer in Burundi despite international trade embargo. (p5)
- Computer company Management Share posted Dfl 0.7 million net last year. (p5) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Insurer Levob lowers mortgage rates by 0.4 pct. (p2)
- Newspaper Het Financieele Dagblad and press agency ANP to set up new financial press service. (p2)
- Unions are positive about solving problems around 276 forced lay-offs of 650 jobs at bulk transhipment company EBS. (p2)
- Union FNV to present steel maker Hoogovens with an ultimatum to reopen talks on pay and conditions. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch marines catch drugs traffickers. (p1)
- Cut price airline EasyJet offers single flight Amsterdam- London for nine guilders. (p1)
- Dutch Tourists Association NBT to present plans to lure tourists back. (p6)
- Liberals in parliament want traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma to take firm measures to prevent unfair competition from PTT in courier market. (p19)
TROUW
- Food and detergent group Unilever's unit Van den Bergh management guarantees jobs and pay after wild cat strike of distribution staff. (p7)
- Machine maker Stork is prepared to take on temp workers in a labour pool. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Engineering company Fugro sells its British, North and South American environmental activities. (p11)
